solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Space in pool for frolicking

indicators.note: the space is placed in the middle of the pool, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money, as in a card game
an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Swimmers have room to play about in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a swimming pool; here 'pool' is a shared fund of money, and 'Space' is the typesetter's en.
explanation.definitionFit: Young cats are famously playful, so an adjective built on them describes frisky, frolicsome behaviour.

clue.text: A dash within, the clue within

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, as in a trace of flavour
a pointer or suggestion that helps someone guess

indicators.note: the closing word tells us the letters lie inside the words just before it

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter muses that a single dash can carry the clue inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'within, the', ignoring the comma. Both 'A dash' and 'clue' define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small trace of something and a suggestive pointer offered to a solver.

clue.text: Story, tall one condensed?

parts.note: a story can be a falsehood, a fib
tall means large or big

explanation.surface: A tall story gets shortened in the retelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Justus von Liebig was the German chemist after whom the Liebig condenser, a piece of laboratory glassware, is named; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemist's name is attached to a laboratory condenser, so he is cheekily described as someone who condensed.

clue.text: Weakness in the end solvers frequently see

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word solvers is wanted, the bit at its end

parts.note: oft is an old word for often
to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: Solvers often see a weakness in a puzzle eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: A fondness or susceptibility for someone or something is a vulnerability, a particular partiality one cannot resist.

clue.text: Toy you shouldn't have received having broken the speed of sound

parts.note: said when thanking someone for a gift, so it means ta, British for thanks

indicators.note: the word for received has broken into the speed of sound, splitting it apart

parts.note: Mach 1, written MACH I, is the speed of sound
got means received

explanation.surface: An unwanted present has broken the sound barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' is the polite reply to a gift, so it stands for thanks. The speed of sound is Mach 1, written with a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamagotchi is a Japanese electronic virtual pet, a handheld plaything that was a 1990s craze.

clue.text: Leader of military uprising, I add in basic info on website, possibly …

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
add is placed inside the website abbreviation

parts.note: FAQ, frequently asked questions, is the basic information page on a website
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel commander's details are added to a website's basic information page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' reads the whole build from the bottom up, as this is a down clue. The ellipsis leads on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Muammar Gaddafi was the Libyan colonel who seized power in a 1969 coup and ruled as the country's military leader.

clue.text: Out to burn, perhaps, is short of good gear in summer?

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to burn is slang for riding fast, so someone out riding a bike is out to burn

explanation.surface: Someone out to get a tan lacks decent summer clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'burn' as sunburn; it is a fast ride. BIKING loses G, then IS is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-piece swimsuits are typical warm-weather beachwear, a kind of clothing worn in the summer months.

clue.text: Compositions produced by a lad at a gate to Shropshire

parts.note: a son is a lad

indicators.note: a gate is the way in, so the first letter of Shropshire is taken

explanation.surface: A boy wrote music at a gateway into the English county of Shropshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonatas are pieces of classical music, typically for one or two instruments in several movements.

clue.text: … where things happen unmoderated, 'fat' creator's sacked

indicators.note: sacked suggests a city plundered and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Following on from the dictator, a portly creator is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FAT CREATORS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor of this kind runs without a moderator to slow the neutrons, so its reactions are literally unmoderated.

clue.text: Bud Street's included in A to Z book

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A street appears in an A to Z street-map book.
explanation.walkthrough: An A to Z is a British street atlas. Read as 'A to B last', Z is the last letter and the book's B slots in before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In freshwater sponges and bryozoans, this is an asexual reproductive body, a kind of resistant bud.

clue.text: What's left in Toughie diagram? I can help

indicators.note: going to the left means reading right to left, backwards
the letters sit inside the words Toughie diagram

explanation.surface: A solver asks what is still blank in the grid and offers to help.
explanation.walkthrough: EDIA spans 'ToughiE DIAgram'; reading it leftwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is someone whose role is to support, so the definition is that helper speaking.

clue.text: Untried name crossword enthusiasts should put about

indicators.note: the solver phrase is put around the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: us, the solvers reading the clue, are the crossword enthusiasts
ought means should

explanation.surface: Crossword fans should spread the word about a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossword enthusiasts' are us, the people solving, a common setter's self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not looked for or attempted has not been tried, a near-synonym for being unsought.

clue.text: Maybe crawling from south of plain, bear with a cut

indicators.note: in a down clue reading from the south means going upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a llano is a grassy South American plain

indicators.note: cut means a letter is removed from the bear's Latin name

parts.note: ursa is Latin for bear, as in Ursa Major

explanation.surface: A bear on a plain with a wound is perhaps seen crawling.
explanation.walkthrough: OF and LLANO read upwards give ONALLFO; URSA loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving on hands and knees is one way to crawl, so the idiom describes crawling as an example.

clue.text: What setter must check for with son

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
of can mean with, as in a man of means

explanation.surface: A setter must check something for, or with, a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Before publication a setter reads trial printed copies of the puzzle to catch errors.

clue.text: A possible cause of death on board, CS tackled in manoeuvres

definitions.text: A possible cause of death on board

indicators.note: the letters are moved about like troops on manoeuvres

explanation.surface: A sailor's fatal accident on deck involved some tackling during manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; it is the Cluedo board, Cluedo being a British murder-mystery board game.
explanation.definitionFit: In the board game Cluedo, this is one of the six weapons with which the victim may have been killed.

clue.text: In singularly drink-induced disorder, welcome bread for Laureate

indicators.note: the welcome and the bread go in the disorder, which surrounds them

parts.note: DTs, delirium tremens, is a drink-induced disorder; singularly drops the S
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting
nan, or naan, is an Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: A drunk poet greets the bread while in a state of delirium.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir William Davenant was a 17th-century English poet who was effectively the second Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Evidence someone's talking about me being out of it?

definitions.text: Evidence someone's talking about me being out of it?

parts.words: Evidence someone's talking about me being out of it?
parts.note: folklore says your ears burn or feel hot when others talk about you, and they gossip when you are beyond hearing range

explanation.surface: Someone suspects they are being gossiped about while away.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as EARS HOT, the sign that you are being discussed; and people talk about you when you are out of hearing range.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the range within which sound can be heard, and gossip happens when the subject is outside it.

clue.text: 2 veg — with which, regularly, meat is served up?

indicators.note: served up suggests food dished out in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
every second letter of meat is taken

explanation.surface: A dinner question: two vegetables, and with which the meat is served.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 2 down. VEG, ET (from 'mEaT') and IS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny remaining trace or suggestion of something matches the 'dash' sense of the earlier answer.

clue.text: Being set back essentially involved a couple cutting out air conditioner

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the letters run backwards
essentially means the central core of the word involved
cutting out means removing the three letters from the couple

parts.note: a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A couple are involved in removing an air conditioner.
explanation.walkthrough: VOLV is the core of 'inVOLVed'; PAIR loses AIR, leaving P. VOLV + A + P read backwards gives the answer. 'Air conditioner' looks like one appliance; 'air' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov conditioned dogs to salivate at the sound of a bell, the founding experiment of classical conditioning.

clue.text: I felt that service should be included in credit for fellow blogger, perhaps

indicators.note: the pain cry and the service go inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: ow is what you say when you feel pain
a rite is a religious service

explanation.surface: A wounded blogger thinks a service should be credited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes jointly with another, as two bloggers might share a post, is a writing partner.

clue.text: Love beginning to solve cryptic with pre-eminent team

indicators.note: cryptic means obscure or puzzling, so these letters are jumbled
only the opening letter of solve is used

explanation.surface: A solver loves starting on a cryptic in company with a top side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' jumbles only LOVE, giving OLVE. Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club, were dominant in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of an English football club that was the leading side in the 1950s, winning the league three times.

clue.text: Pairs of performers look to be missing Dutch city

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letters for Dutch go

parts.note: duos are pairs of performers
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Pairs of performers look as if they have lost the Dutch city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch city' looks like the definition, but Dutch is the DU removed from DUOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Norway is a Scandinavian capital, which the clue simply calls a city.

clue.text: By which to 'largely' advertise one working out last of down answers?

indicators.note: working something out means reworking it, so the three letters are rearranged
only the final letter of the word down is taken

parts.note: lights are crossword answers, the entries in the grid

explanation.surface: A solver working out the last of the down answers wants to tell the world in big letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To advertise something in glowing illuminated signs is to publicise it hugely, as a name up in lights.

clue.text: Move on — without husband, it's clarified

indicators.note: without means outside, so the urging word goes around the husband

parts.note: gee, or gee up, urges a horse to move on

explanation.surface: Someone told to move on without a husband says things are now clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: This South Asian cooking fat is butter that has been heated and strained, i.e. clarified butter.

clue.text: What painter's used for gold one little chap's endlessly taken aback about

indicators.note: the reversed little man goes about the gold and the one
taken aback suggests something pulled backwards, so the letters run in reverse
endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a gnome is a little man of folklore
the final letter of the little man's word is dropped
OR is gold in heraldry
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An artist puts gold leaf on a startled small man.
explanation.walkthrough: A painter is a rope used to tie up a boat, not an artist. GNOM read backwards is MONG, which wraps ORI.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's painter is the line used to tie it up at a quay, which is the act of securing it in place.

clue.text: An eye for an eye, say — not for turning

indicators.note: turning means the letters are turned around, read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
never means not ever, not at all

explanation.surface: An eye-for-an-eye stance, say, is not for turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not for turning' echoes Margaret Thatcher's 'The lady's not for turning'. EG + NEVER is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical retribution in kind, injury for injury, is the classic expression of getting even with a wrongdoer.
